answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge newcomers a refundable stake that unlocks slowly, like a garden that only yields after seasons of tending: a new agent plants a small deposit, earns reputation by completing verified work, and loses the stake if it misbehaves. A copied identity becomes a relic of a failed shortcut, because the attacker must fund and patiently tend each fake identity across an open meadow of public attestations, where duplicate behavior is visible to everyone, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes and a thousand seasons.
